Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.factory

Class Factory<M extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.factory.Factory<M>
Type Parameters:
M - the model type
public abstract class Factory<M extends Model> extends Object
Builds models, or raw attribute rows, from a base definition and layered states.

Build one with of(ModelQuery, Supplier), or extend this class and implement definition(); a subclass names its states in its own methods that return Factory<M>. Every fluent call returns a new factory and leaves the receiver unchanged, so a factory is immutable and safe to share across threads.

The definition and each state are maps from attribute names to values. A value that is a Supplier is called with no argument, and a value that is a Function is called with a read-only snapshot of the attributes built so far; the result is used as is and is not resolved again, except that a result that is a factory or a model is expanded as a nested value. A ClassCastException thrown while a value is resolved is rethrown as an IllegalArgumentException that names the attribute and the model class, never the value, with the original as its cause.

make, create, createQuietly and raw build exactly one and ignore count(int). The *Many() methods and insert() build as many as count says, or one when it was not set; the variants taking a number use that number. Each model's position starts at zero on every call.

Diwan has no fake data: every value comes from the definition, a state or a sequence. create throws when a save is stopped or stores no row, where ModelQuery.create(Map) returns the unsaved model. insert sends one statement, so the binding limit of the database applies (999 on SQLite before 3.32), and rows with different key sets make it throw an IllegalArgumentException.

Relations: has(Factory, String) and hasAttached(Factory, String) create children after each created model is saved, and forParent(Factory, String) gives a model its parent first. A value in the attributes that is a factory creates its model and stores the key, and a value that is a model stores its key. recycle(Model...) lets a call reuse saved models instead of creating parents, and withoutParents() turns nested factory values into null. Every terminal call builds one run context that holds the recycle position and the random generator, so two calls on one factory share nothing and the factory stays immutable. make creates the parents but never the children, insert creates the parents and skips the children and the hooks, and raw never touches the database. There is no transaction: rows already written stay when a later one fails.

    • has

      public Factory<M> has(Factory<? extends Model> child, String relation)
      Returns a factory that creates children under each created model, through a has-one, has-many, morph-one or morph-many relation.

      The children are created after the model is saved, with the key column (and the type column of a morph relation) set last, so it wins over the child's own states. The child factory keeps its own count, states and hooks, and its parent-aware states and hooks receive the saved model. Nothing is created by make, insert or raw.

      Parameters:
      child - the factory of the children, never null
      relation - the relation name on this model, never null
      Returns:
      a new factory, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - when a create call runs, if the relation is not one of the four kinds
      RelationNotFoundException - when a create call runs, if the model has no relation of that name
      IllegalStateException - when a create call runs, if the saved model has no value for the local key

    • forParent

      public Factory<M> forParent(Factory<? extends Model> parent, String relation)
      Returns a factory whose models belong to a parent that a factory creates, through a belongs-to or morph-to relation. This is the relation's "for", named forParent because for is a Java keyword.

      The parent is created before the model, once for the whole call whatever the count, unless the recycle pool holds a model of its class. The key column, and the type column of a morph-to relation, are set before the states, so a state can override them. A recycled model must be saved. raw throws, because it never touches the database.

      Parameters:
      parent - the factory of the parent, never null
      relation - the belongs-to or morph-to relation name on this model, never null
      Returns:
      a new factory, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - when a terminal call runs, if the relation is not belongs-to or morph-to
      IllegalStateException - when raw or rawMany runs

    • forParent

      public void insert()
      Inserts as many rows as the count says, or one, in one statement. No after-making or after-creating hook and no model event runs, though beforeWrite() runs on each row, and no row is sent when the count is below 1.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the rows do not have the same keys
      QueryException - if the database refuses the insert
